production PostgreSQL representation/transport/copy detail adapter: rows on the application connection, durable before the first byte, naming the delivery's B2 record and the request; a row that connection refused is written as the effect of the delivery's terminal operation on its ledger transaction, before the terminal event, with the first failure's cause (retained_after), so a terminal event exists only with every response's facts retained, and a closing the ledger refuses is that operation's journaled rollback (B2 failure journal, the admitted terminal event naming the delivery) whose rows the service keeps for the next close or shutdown (R244-GPT-02); a failed preparation's copy observation is found from its record through its own delivery link (R244-GPT-03)

per-response source checks outside the ledger lane: the study's current identity (OrthancService.studyPatientIdentity, the same read and rule as D's current study: no resource, two patient resources under the UID, the one patient) and the selected object's current PatientID, both against the manifest's patient, before any body read; a split UID or a correction refuses the response and forgets the kept manifest (R244-GPT-01)
each exact study-manifest body is kept once (emr_image.source_manifest) and every preparation names it; earlier preparations keep their own copy (R244-02)

the access record of viewing (의료법 제23조④) is the study delivery (emr-image/delivery.ts): one B2 provide-prepared event per requester, rights, session, address and manifest version, admitted/committed/confirmed before the delivery's first response is prepared, closed by one terminal event (ended, aborted, or none for an unconfirmed ending) after a short idle period, a bounded age, a changed current fact or shutdown; each response checks the requester's current access on one bounded transaction of E's own check pool (check-db.ts: the same database and role, eight connections apart from the application pool and the ledger's lanes) before any source read (a response appends nothing; the ledger's lanes carry the delivery's opening and closing) and keeps its fixed representation, transport and copy facts in emr_image rows naming that event (X-KIN-Image-Event the record, X-KIN-Image-Response the row; 20261027090000_emr_e_study_delivery); earlier rows are their own record (R244-02 throughput)

served CT frame throughput through E (R244-02): with every frame response its own B2 access record a frame held the 4 append lanes 233 ms median (run e-route-diag2-opus-20261026a). The record is now the study delivery (20261027090000): per frame one bounded ledger transaction for the current access check and plan, the frame's own rows on the application connection, no admission, append or terminal event per frame. Same VM, same 200 x 512x512 CT, both integrated with #248 c99f45b (runs e-route-before-fable-20261027a on 1a95c94, e-route-after-fable-20261027a on bb2b3c8): first opening 9.1 s first image / 19.4 s all frames before, 10.5 / 17.3 s after; repeated opening 4.1 / 14.5 s before, 4.2 / 11.6 s after (19.3 -> 27.2 frames/s after the first image), against 4.2 / 7.8 s direct (e-route-red3-opus-20261026a). The per-stage profile (run e-route-diag-fable-20261027a, 405 responses, medians) showed the four lanes saturated again: the identity admission waited 222 ms and the one ledger transaction 285 ms, with D's per-frame current read running an Orthanc QIDO inside the lane while Orthanc serves the frames; staging 126 ms; the viewer keeps about 20 frames in flight. With the per-response re-check (ImageContextSource.recheck, 323a259: D's scope read and the provision on the lane, the archive's patient identity read once per delivery opening; run e-route-after2-fable-20261027a on fd12aef = 323a259 + #248): first opening 11.3 / 17.8 s, repeated 4.3 / 10.6 s (32.0 frames/s). A repeated opening is 1.36x direct and a first opening 2.2x: not the 1.2x the throughput order asked for. What a frame still pays: the request identity's own append admission (B2), one bounded ledger transaction (D resolves the identity twice, reads StudyState, the StudyAccess snapshot and the FOR SHARE scope), the staging copy and hash of the frame (the same archive read the direct route pays), and three application-connection inserts; the first opening also waits for the whole-study catalog read (#248)
